rows.title: ‘I’m Still Here’ Review: Walter Salles’ Profoundly Moving Sense-Memory Portrait of a Family — and a Nation — Ruptured
rows.comment: Classical in form but radical in empathy
rows.verdict_le10: Classical in form but radical in empathy
rows.dek_lead: Classical in form but radical in empathy, “I’m Still Here” arguably does not need the follow-up sections — one set in 1996 and the other in 2014 — that somewhat alter the emotional rhythm.

rows.title: 'I'm Still Here' Review: Walter Salles' Powerful Drama of Resistance
rows.comment: profoundly touching film with a deep well of pathos
rows.verdict_le10: profoundly touching film with a deep well of pathos
rows.dek_lead: While it could use a less generic international title that’s not also a well-known Stephen Sondheim song, I’m Still Here is a gripping, profoundly touching film with a deep well of pathos. It’s one of Salles’ best.

rows.title: I’m Still Here review – wrenching true-life saga of a Brazilian family torn apart by military rule | Drama films
rows.comment: the picture represents Salles at his absolute best.
rows.verdict_le10: the picture represents Salles at his absolute best.
rows.dek_lead: Meticulous in its period detail, I’m Still Here unfolds in a vividly evoked early 1970s Rio, with two later chapters set in 1996 and 2014. Far-reaching in its themes, the picture represents Salles at his absolute best.

rows.title: I’m Still Here review: Walter Salles’s poignant, personal vision of family life under fascism
rows.comment: Like a pat on the family sofa that beckons you over to join the throng
rows.verdict_le10: Like a pat on the family sofa that beckons you over to join the throng
rows.dek_lead: And like it, I’m Still Here takes you right into the machinery of a repressive regime, showing just enough of its dank jail cells and casual cruelties without overwhelming its deeper story of loss. Like a pat on the family sofa that beckons
